title: Install Paperboy and select renderer schedules
summary: Install Paperboy, initialize its TOML manifest, apply per-job Clockwork snapshots, and explicitly enable or disable selected renderer jobs.
use_when: Install or update Paperboy, initialize or validate its manifest, publish configured schedules, inspect schedule selection, or control one selected job.
do_not_use_when: The request is to execute a job now, retry a saved email, modify another product, or infer inbox delivery.
outcome: Matching Paperboy programs and provider bytes are selected; configured jobs have exact Clockwork schedule selections with preserved existing enabled intent and new jobs disabled.
effects: Installation selects matching program and provider files, initializes only a missing default manifest, and applies configured schedule snapshots. It does not execute renderers or send their output.

Apply registers all definitions before binding changes, preserves existing enabled intent, leaves new jobs disabled, and disables removed jobs without deleting history or incidents. Explicit enable permits future renderer executions and email.
authority: Paperboy owns its manifest and schedule selection. Clockwork owns atomic per-key transitions, runtime history, overlap and failure halts. Cell deployment owns instruction execution and retained receipts; renderer and Email success remain separate.
success: Initialization succeeds when the absent manifest is written or existing valid configuration is preserved. Apply succeeds after every requested selection and removal transition completes. Installation succeeds when declared instructions complete. None establishes renderer correctness, future timer delivery, or inbox receipt.
failure_and_recovery: Multi-job apply is not atomic. Earlier successful transitions remain after a later failure. Inspect schedule status, correct the reported problem, and reapply the same manifest. Retain Clockwork history and established incidents.
Failed deployment retains completed effects and executes no automatic rollback or recovery. Inspect retained evidence before an explicitly authorized new attempt.
An established scheduling halt requires exact incident approval through Clockwork. Enable, disable, apply, and installation do not clear it. Approval does not retry a renderer or uncertain email.
privacy: Manifests, schedule arguments, paths, subjects, and logs are private local data. Clockwork retains activation metadata, not renderer bodies.
does_not_authorize: Catalog presence does not authorize installation, enabling a renderer job, deleting retained state, retrying email, or clearing a failure incident.

consumers.statement: The current user and authorized Cell product-deployment operations.

preconditions.statement: Select committed source and required dependency updates explicitly. Schedule operations require installed Paperboy and supported Clockwork. Script execution and schedule enable require separate standing authority.

inputs.statement: An absolute --manifest path or the default manifest and literal configured job definitions. Enable and disable require one job ID; status accepts an optional ID. Init writes an empty version-one manifest only if absent. Installation accepts no product settings and always uses the default manifest. The selected manifest governs the complete paperboy/ binding namespace; alternate paths do not isolate bindings.

outputs.statement: Configured-job validation, immutable definition selections, binding enabled and halt metadata, aggregate local status evidence, and retained deployment instruction outcomes. These observations do not run a renderer.

data_semantics.statement: The manifest is configuration authority; applied definitions are scheduled command snapshots. Existing jobs retain enabled intent, new jobs are disabled, and removed jobs retain disabled selection and history. Status represents retained binding metadata rather than guaranteed future activation. Scheduled logs can retain result metadata, including an accepted provider message ID, but no body or structured send-recovery ledger.

identity_and_units.statement: Each stable manifest ID maps to paperboy/JOB_ID. Changing its configuration changes the immutable definition; renaming it creates a different binding. Durations use whole seconds and calendar schedules use the host local hour and minute.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Apply validates all configured jobs and registers their definitions before binding mutations. Status reads selected Clockwork metadata at invocation. The product aggregate status-snapshot describes configuration and readiness, not each dynamic binding or execution history. Initialization validates and preserves an existing manifest rather than replacing it.
No maximum activation delay, catch-up count, or final email-delivery latency is promised.

access.statement: Current-user local interfaces use the provider-owned Clockwork and Email clients. Scheduled definitions launch the exact installed Paperboy program from the product root; renderer launch context is defined by paperboy.report.send. launchd schedule delivery requires a macOS GUI login domain.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: One schedule lock serializes Paperboy mutations. Clockwork provides per-key transition atomicity; multi-job apply retains earlier completed transitions after failure. Identical selections need no transition. Disable retains definitions and incidents, and no apply enables a new job.

operational_limits.statement: Manifest maximum 1 MiB. Per-job schedules use overlap skip, run-at-load false, and a 1380-second outer timeout. Different jobs can run concurrently. Interval range is 1 through 31536000 seconds; local hour 0 through 23 and minute 0 through 59. Logs append under the private Paperboy logs directory.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Installation selects manifest job schedules. The version-one TOML manifest is the configuration authority. Product installation and Clockwork selection remain separate from renderer execution.
No general future compatibility or deprecation window is promised.

reliances.statement: The Paperboy renderer feature defines manifest input, execution, exact stdout handoff, email success, privacy, and limits.
Clockwork supplies definition registration, exact binding transitions, scheduling, overlap, runtime records, incidents, and continuation approval.
Email supplies the selected fixed-recipient wrapper and submission boundary; applying a schedule does not test credentials or send.
Cell deployment executes explicitly selected product instructions and retains completed or unknown effects. It infers no application recovery or rollback.
